specific_names: Public disclosure would erode strategy value
destruction of restructuring balance of power
judge only access invites access demands

claims.claim: Requiring hedge funds to supply risk and valuation data in a simplified format would in fact impose a significant burden on the industry, since simplification requirements would raise transaction costs, require pre-screening, and possibly additional staff.
conditions: where the SEC prescribes a simplified reporting format
claims.source: Hedge Fund Valuation Retailization, Regulation, and Investor Suitability
claims.quote: In addition to the utilization problem, if the SEC should require hedge funds to provide risk and valuation data in a certain simplified format, the SEC would in fact impose a significant burden on the hedge fund industry.
claims.citation: Kaal, Hedge Fund Valuation Retailization, Regulation, and Investor Suitability (2009). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1428387

claims.claim: Where the Form PF quarterly reporting threshold does influence behavior, it distorts fund size downward: a majority of the advisers who take the threshold into account plan to stay under $1.5 billion in assets under management, and some would close funds to new investors to do so.
conditions: the 19.54% of respondents who would take the Form PF threshold into account
claims.source: Hedge Fund Manager Registration Under the Dodd-Frank Act
claims.quote: A majority of those respondents who would take it into account plan to stay under the Form PF threshold for quarterly reporting of $1.5 billion AUM.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Hedge Fund Manager Registration Under the Dodd-Frank Act (2012). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2150377

claims.claim: Restricting Form PF data to the eyes of the bankruptcy judge alone would create problems in the litigation process, because opposing parties may demand access to the same information.
claims.specific_name: judge only access invites access demands
claims.source: Hedge Funds’ Systemic Risk Disclosures in Bankruptcy
claims.quote: However, making creditors' Form PF data available for the eyes of the judge only could raise issues in the litigation process because parties may demand access to the same information.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Hedge Funds’ Systemic Risk Disclosures in Bankruptcy (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2348463

claims.claim: Increased disclosure obligations let so-called pilot fish emulate hedge funds' investment strategies and positions, which makes those positions more expensive to build and strips systematic bargaining strength from the negotiation process.
conditions: markets where competitors can observe and copy disclosed positions
claims.source: Hedge Funds’ Systemic Risk Disclosures in Bankruptcy
claims.quote: disclosure obligations, "pilot fish" can increasingly emulate investment strategies and positions. As a result, investment positions can become more expensive and systematic bargaining strength is removed from the negotiation process.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Hedge Funds’ Systemic Risk Disclosures in Bankruptcy (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2348463

claims.claim: There is a real risk that increased disclosure through Form PF would destroy the balance of power in the restructuring process.
claims.specific_name: destruction of restructuring balance of power
conditions: if Form PF data were introduced into the bankruptcy process
claims.source: Hedge Funds’ Systemic Risk Disclosures in Bankruptcy
claims.quote: In summary, there is a real risk that increased disclosures via Form PF would destroy the balance of power in the restructuring process.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Hedge Funds’ Systemic Risk Disclosures in Bankruptcy (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2348463

claims.claim: Form PF's counterparty credit exposure requirement is difficult to satisfy at the source, because the exposure is highly sensitive information that individual fund managers often cannot readily determine.
conditions: Form PF counterparty credit exposure disclosures
claims.source: Private Fund Disclosures Under the Dodd-Frank Act
claims.quote: For instance, the disclosure of counterparty credit exposure is sensitive information that can often not readily be determined by the individual fund managers.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Private Fund Disclosures Under the Dodd-Frank Act (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2447306

claims.claim: Asked what the SEC should fix first, respondents named the burdensome nature and the ambiguity of Form PF as the most pressing issues, not the substance of what is disclosed.
claims.source: Private Fund Disclosures Under the Dodd-Frank Act
claims.quote: Respondents identified the burdensome nature and the ambiguity of Form PF as the most pressing issues with Form PF.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Private Fund Disclosures Under the Dodd-Frank Act (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2447306

claims.claim: For a substantial minority, existing systems fail Form PF for a specific reason: 34.78 percent of respondents said their internal reporting systems were insufficient because the required answers demand further analysis and calculation beyond what the systems already produce.
conditions: responses to survey Question 15 and follow-up 15b
claims.source: Private Fund Disclosures Under the Dodd-Frank Act
claims.quote: Several respondents (34.78%) opined that their existing internal reporting systems were insufficient to respond to questions on Form PF because they require further analysis and calculations.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Private Fund Disclosures Under the Dodd-Frank Act (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2447306

claims.claim: Working with a service provider imposes its own costs: filers reported that the arrangement requires investing time and money to develop interaction processes and bearing the burden of supplying the provider with the underlying information.
conditions: respondents who used a service provider
claims.source: Private Fund Disclosures Under the Dodd-Frank Act
claims.quote: Commenters identified several challenges in working with a service-provider, including the investment of time and expenses to develop processes, and the burden of providing service-providers with the required information.
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Private Fund Disclosures Under the Dodd-Frank Act (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2447306

claims.claim: The private fund industry's central fear about Form PF was not the filing itself but eventual publicity: if the disclosures ever became public, competitors could reverse engineer fund strategies and largely eliminate managers' ability to generate absolute returns.
claims.specific_name: Public disclosure would erode strategy value
conditions: Form PF disclosures held confidentially by the SEC
claims.source: Private Investment Fund Regulation - Theory and Empirical Evidence from 1998 to 2016
claims.quote: the industry feared that such information could at some point in the future be made public which would largely eliminate private investment fund managers' ability to make absolute returns for their clients as competitors would be able to reverse engineer their strategies. Apart
claims.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Private Investment Fund Regulation - Theory and Empirical Evidence from 1998 to 2016 (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2998097
